name: Asylum / International Protection

qualifying_event.description: The Finnish Immigration Service (Migri) decides on applications for international protection, in a 3-phase process: application (declare intent to police/border authorities/Migri), registration (within 5 days), and lodging the application with supporting grounds (within 21 days of registration; within 5 days under the border procedure).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Registration certificate; grounds for protection presented at the Migri meeting; supporting documents.

requirements.blocker_text: Migri assesses whether the applicant qualifies for refugee status (asylum) or the lesser subsidiary protection status, based on the grounds and evidence presented.
Must be within Finnish territory to apply for international protection in Finland.

evidence_required.document: Grounds for protection and supporting documentation

outcome.duration_length: Refugee status: 3-year first/extended permit (reduced from 4 years); Subsidiary protection: 1-year first permit, 2-year extended permit (both reduced effective 2 January 2025)

sources.title: Maahanmuuttovirasto -- Asylum in Finland: 3-phase application process (application, registration within 5 days, lodging within 21 days), right to work and study during processing, reception-centre housing

Maahanmuuttovirasto -- The Validity Periods of International Protection Permits Will Be Shortened and Protection Becomes Temporary, effective 2 January 2025: refugee permits 4yr to 3yr; subsidiary protection first permit to 1yr, extended permit 4yr to 2yr
Maahanmuuttovirasto -- Subsidiary Protection: definition, 1-year initial permit, unrestricted work rights, family reunification access

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Finland). MAJOR REFORM, effective 2 January 2025 (already in force): Finland shortened international-protection permit validity periods as part of a shift toward treating protection as temporary and requiring more frequent reassessment (refugee status 4yr to 3yr; subsidiary protection extended permit 4yr to 2yr, first permit newly set at just 1yr). This is a genuinely tier-1-sourced, well-documented reform (unlike several international_protection.json builds elsewhere in this dataset that rely on tier-2 UNHCR sourcing), so this file is PUBLISHED rather than draft. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months use the general fi_permanent_residence.json / fi_naturalisation.json figures; no protection-specific reduced naturalisation track (e.g. a stateless/refugee-specific shortcut) was confirmed in this pass -- flagged as a possible gap, not modeled as guaranteed.
